solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: New tree shoot outside? It's that time of year!

indicators.note: the shoot sits outside the letter for new, so it wraps round it

parts.note: a sprig is a small shoot or twig from a tree or plant

explanation.surface: A gardener spots fresh growth on a tree and announces the season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' puts SPRIG round N.
explanation.definitionFit: The season of new growth is the time of year the exclamation points to, after winter ends.

clue.text: When the curtain goes up, directs how Tim enunciates lines

indicators.note: the answer lies within the line of words, so its letters run through directS HOW TIM Enunciates

explanation.surface: A director shows how an actor called Tim should speak his lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lines' points to the answer running through directS HOW TIM Enunciates.
explanation.definitionFit: The moment a performance starts is the time the show begins, when the stage is revealed.

clue.text: There's quite a lot of it in Llanfair, unfortunately

definitions.text: There's quite a lot of it

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things going wrong, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A grumble about Welsh weather in the village of Llanfair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' rearranges LLANFAIR. Wales is famously wet.
explanation.definitionFit: Precipitation is plentiful in Wales, so there is a great deal of it in a Welsh village.

clue.text: Number of female swans flying from northern uplands

indicators.note: flying from means leaving, so these letters are taken out of the hills' name

parts.note: the Pennines are a range of hills in northern England
a pen is a female swan

explanation.surface: A count of swans taking off from the northern hills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flying from' removes P, E, N and S from PENNINES. The Pennines are the hill range down the middle of northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Nine is a whole number, the integer that comes after eight.

clue.text: Pushing around small vessels

indicators.note: pushed around means jumbled about, so the letters of the first word are rearranged

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing sizes

explanation.surface: Someone shoving little boats about in the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pushing around' reads as a phrase, but 'around' is the anagram signal on PUSHING, giving GUNSHIP before the S for small.
explanation.definitionFit: Armed boats or helicopters carrying guns are craft, so plural warships fit the plural word vessels.

clue.text: Steadfast auntie's night off

indicators.note: off means out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A determined aunt takes an evening off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges AUNTIES NIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting without wavering or delay shows a firm, resolute spirit.

clue.text: Having this, one suffers fools gladly!

definitions.text: Having this, one suffers fools gladly!

parts.words: Having this, one suffers fools gladly
parts.note: a fool is a fruit-and-cream pudding, so someone fond of sugary food happily puts up with them

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'suffers fools gladly' means tolerates idiots; here a fool is a creamy British fruit dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: Fondness for sugary food is the craving that makes eating desserts a pleasure.

clue.text: One from the sub-continent turning up to help in pub

indicators.note: in places the reversed help inside the pub

parts.note: an inn is a pub

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up reads the word upward, so backwards

parts.note: to aid is to help

explanation.surface: Someone from South Asia arrives to lend a hand at the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' makes DIA from AID and 'in' places it in INN.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of India comes from the Indian subcontinent.

clue.text: Guitarist leaving Turkey when it's hot

indicators.note: leaving means departing, so the country's code is removed

parts.note: a strummer plays guitar; Joe Strummer was the Clash guitarist
TR is the international code for Turkey

explanation.surface: A guitarist leaves Turkey because it is too hot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' removes TR from STRUMMER.
explanation.definitionFit: The warmest season of the year is the time of heat.

clue.text: Leg irons jailor finally removed — they make me cry

parts.note: ON is the leg side in cricket

indicators.note: removed says a letter is taken out of the word irons
finally points to the closing letter of the word jailor

explanation.surface: A prisoner, finally freed of leg irons by the jailer, weeps with relief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes R from jailor and 'removed' deletes it from IRONS, leaving IONS. The leg side in cricket is called the on side.
explanation.definitionFit: Chopping these bulbs releases a compound that stings the eyes and makes the cook weep.

clue.text: Caught husband that is following mod round boss's office

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
i.e. abbreviates id est, Latin for that is
F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

indicators.note: turning round reads the word mod backwards

parts.note: taken as written: a mod is a 1960s youth who rode scooters

explanation.surface: A husband is caught chasing a 1960s mod around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' looks like a link word but supplies F; 'round' turns the mod backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The suffix -dom names a position or realm, so a leader's rank or territory is the post of the person in charge.

clue.text: Time to get into mama's softer new bed?

indicators.note: to get into means to go inside, so this letter goes within the rearranged letters
new means remade, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Time for Mum to buy a softer new bed?
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges MAMAS SOFTER and 'to get into' puts T inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A mattress made of foam is a bed, or the main part of one.

clue.text: Express disapproval about fine cluster of threads

indicators.note: about means going round, so the disapproving sound surrounds the abbreviation

parts.note: to tut is to click the tongue in disapproval
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil grades

explanation.surface: Someone tutting over a nice little bunch of threads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts TUT round F.
explanation.definitionFit: A tuft is a small bunch of yarn, hair or grass growing or held together at the base.

clue.text: An exchange of punches in political negotiations?

definitions.meaning: a Suffolk Punch is a breed of heavy draught horse, so swapping punches is dealing in horses
hard bargaining with concessions traded, as between parties forming a coalition

explanation.walkthrough: 'punches' looks like blows in a fight; it means Suffolk Punch horses, a British breed of heavy farm horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrewd bargaining in politics borrows its name from the haggling of dealers buying and selling livestock.

clue.text: Beating my record on titanium piercing

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like my!

indicators.note: piercing means going through, so the metal's symbol goes inside

parts.note: rec is short for record
Ti is the chemical symbol for titanium

explanation.surface: An athlete is surprised to see a personal best beaten by a titanium-assisted rival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beating' looks like breaking a record but is the definition, an old sense of punishment. 'piercing' puts the metal into record-plus-on. Cor! is a British cry of surprise, like my!
explanation.definitionFit: Correction is an old word for punishment, especially a thrashing given to a wrongdoer.

clue.text: Crookedness of an immortal criminal

indicators.note: criminal suggests something bent or wrong, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A wicked god's moral crookedness is condemned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' rearranges OF AN IMMORTAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A deformity is a body part being misshapen or bent, which is crookedness in a physical sense.

clue.text: Labour left American mother Jenny oddly cut on belly

parts.note: mom is American for mother

indicators.note: oddly cut means the odd letters of the name are cut away, leaving the even ones

parts.note: tum is a belly

explanation.surface: A left-wing American mother called Jenny gets a cut on her stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly cut' removes J, N and Y to leave EN. Momentum is a left-wing campaign group inside Britain's Labour Party.
explanation.definitionFit: The group was founded to back Jeremy Corbyn and is the organised left faction of the party.

clue.text: Charlie beginning to like more expensive clothes, he asserts

indicators.note: clothes is a verb here, dressing or wrapping round the letters

parts.note: dearer means more expensive
C is Charlie in the NATO alphabet

indicators.note: beginning to points to the opening letter of like

explanation.surface: Charlie begins to fancy pricier clothes, he says.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothes' puts DEARER round C and L.
explanation.definitionFit: One who declares is a person who states or announces something firmly.

clue.text: Spooner's agitated, skint — this could follow a plunge

indicators.note: Spooner's signals that the opening sounds of two words are swapped

parts.note: stressed means anxious and agitated
skint is British slang for having no money, i.e. broke

explanation.surface: A worried, penniless man is about to jump in.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of STRESSED BROKE gives BREAST STROKE. Skint is British slang for penniless.
explanation.definitionFit: After diving into a pool a swimmer may set off with this front stroke, so it can come after a plunge.

clue.text: Fall over in Britain?

parts.note: the American season of fall has a different name over the Atlantic in Britain

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fall over' looks like tumbling down; it is the American name for a season, as it is called over in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Americans call the season between summer and winter fall; the British name it differently.

clue.text: Conservative quits (splits departs)

indicators.note: quits means walks out of, so the party's letter is removed from the word for splits

parts.note: cleaves means splits, as an axe does wood

explanation.surface: A Tory resigns, the party splits, and he walks out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quits' removes C from CLEAVES. The brackets make the clue look like a list of synonyms.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who goes away from a place walks out of it, and the same verb also means exits.

clue.text: A French former partner reportedly viewing flat

parts.note: un is French for a
an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so a word that sounds like this one is used

parts.note: a sighting is a viewing of something

explanation.surface: Seeing a Frenchman's ex-partner while flat-hunting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' replaces SIGHTING with its sound-alike CITING.
explanation.definitionFit: Something flat lacks sparkle or interest, so it is dull and fails to thrill.

clue.text: Clubs withdrawing from transfer agreement

indicators.note: withdrawing from says the card suit's letter is taken out

parts.note: a decal is a transfer, a design moved from paper onto a surface
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

explanation.surface: A football club pulls out of a transfer deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'withdrawing from' removes C from DECAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A deal is an arrangement or bargain struck between two parties.

clue.text: Dad touring island location with listed building

indicators.note: touring means going round, so dad goes round the island's letters

parts.note: pa is dad

explanation.surface: Father tours an island with a historic building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touring' puts dad round the island. 'listed' looks like heritage status; it means leaning.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian city has the famous Leaning Tower; a ship that lists leans to one side.

clue.text: Vile nude sculpture exposed

indicators.note: a sculpture is shaped or moulded, so the letters are reworked into a new form

explanation.surface: An obscene naked statue is put on show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sculpture' rearranges VILE NUDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking the cover off reveals something, so uncovered means laid bare or exposed.

clue.text: Visiting Krakow in terribly cold time of year

indicators.note: visiting means staying within, so the letters are found inside these words

explanation.surface: A tourist finds Krakow dreadfully chilly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Visiting' finds the answer inside kraKOW IN TERribly.
explanation.definitionFit: The coldest season of the year comes between autumn and spring.

clue.text: Number functions start to satisfy an inquisitive nature

parts.note: sine is a trigonometric function

indicators.note: start to points to the opening letter of the word satisfy

explanation.surface: Maths functions begin to satisfy a curious mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start to' takes S from satisfy.
explanation.definitionFit: Being prying or overly curious about others is an inquisitive nature.

clue.text: Fighting Julius, Resistance is getting closer

parts.note: war is fighting
the setter Julius refers to himself, giving me
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: The setter fights on while the Resistance closes in.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often name themselves to mean ME.
explanation.definitionFit: In the children's game of hot and cold, a seeker nearing the hidden object is told they are getting hotter.
